requirements.quote:
A client stops both sending and processing Initial packets when it
   sends its first Handshake packet.  A server stops sending and
   processing Initial packets when it receives its first Handshake
   packet.  Though packets might still be in flight or awaiting
   acknowledgment, no further Initial packets need to be exchanged
   beyond this point.  Initial packet protection keys are discarded (see
   Section 4.9.1 of [QUIC-TLS]) along with any loss recovery and
   congestion control state; see Section 6.4 of [QUIC-RECOVERY].
requirements.condition: When a client sends its first Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The client stops sending and processing Initial packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not subsequently send or process Initial packets.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-processing and transmission traces can verify that both Initial-packet activities stop at the specified client transition.

requirements.condition: When a server receives its first Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The server stops sending and processing Initial packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not subsequently send or process Initial packets.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-processing and transmission traces can verify that both Initial-packet activities stop at the specified server transition.

requirements.condition: When the endpoint reaches its stated point for abandoning Initial packets.
requirements.required_behavior: Discard Initial packet protection keys.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Retaining usable Initial packet protection keys beyond this point is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: Implementation state can be inspected to determine whether Initial protection keys are removed at the transition.

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Retaining Initial-packet loss-recovery state is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's Initial packet-number-space loss-recovery state can be inspected after key discard.

requirements.quote:
Any data in CRYPTO frames is discarded -- and no longer retransmitted
   -- when Initial keys are discarded.
requirements.required_behavior: Discard data from CRYPTO frames associated with the Initial keys.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Retaining that CRYPTO-frame data is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: Queued CRYPTO data can be inspected at the Initial-key-discard transition.

requirements.quote:

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not retransmit the discarded CRYPTO-frame data.
requirements.why_checkable: Transmission traces can verify that the affected CRYPTO data is never retransmitted after key discard.

requirements.quote:
A 0-RTT packet uses long headers with a type value of 0x01, followed
   by the Length and Packet Number fields; see Section 17.2.  The first
   byte contains the Reserved and Packet Number Length bits; see
   Section 17.2.  A 0-RTT packet is used to carry "early" data from the
   client to the server as part of the first flight, prior to handshake
   completion.  As part of the TLS handshake, the server can accept or
   reject this early data.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a long header with packet type value 0x01.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encoding a 0-RTT packet with another header form or type value is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: The header form and packet type are directly observable in the encoded packet.

requirements.quote:
A 0-RTT packet uses long headers with a type value of 0x01, followed
   by the Length and Packet Number fields; see Section 17.2.  The first
   byte contains the Reserved and Packet Number Length bits; see
   Section 17.2.  A 0-RTT packet is used to carry "early" data from the
   client to the server as part of the first flight, prior to handshake
   completion.  As part of the TLS handshake, the server can accept or
   reject this early data.
requirements.required_behavior: Place the Length field and then the Packet Number field after the long-header fields.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omitting or reversing these fields is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: A packet parser can verify field presence and order in the wire encoding.

requirements.quote:
A 0-RTT packet uses long headers with a type value of 0x01, followed

   byte contains the Reserved and Packet Number Length bits; see

requirements.condition: When encoding the first byte of a 0-RTT packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Reserved bits and Packet Number Length bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omitting either bit field from the first byte is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: The two bit fields are directly observable in the first encoded byte.

requirements.quote:
A 0-RTT packet uses long headers with a type value of 0x01, followed
   by the Length and Packet Number fields; see Section 17.2.  The first

   Section 17.2.  A 0-RTT packet is used to carry "early" data from the

requirements.condition: When a client sends application data in a 0-RTT packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Send it from client to server as early data in the first flight before handshake completion.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a 0-RTT packet for server-to-client data or data sent after handshake completion is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: Endpoint role, flight position, and handshake state can be correlated with each transmitted 0-RTT packet.

requirements.quote:
0-RTT Packet {
     Header Form (1) = 1,
     Fixed Bit (1) = 1,
     Long Packet Type (2) = 1,
     Reserved Bits (2),
     Packet Number Length (2),
     Version (32),
     Destination Connection ID Length (8),
     Destination Connection ID (0..160),
     Source Connection ID Length (8),
     Source Connection ID (0..160),
     Length (i),
     Packet Number (8..32),
     Packet Payload (8..),
   }
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Header Form as a 1-bit field with value 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Any other Header Form value is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and value can be checked directly from the packet bytes.

requirements.quote:
Packet numbers for 0-RTT protected packets use the same space as
   1-RTT protected packets.
requirements.condition: When assigning or tracking packet numbers for 0-RTT protected packets.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the same packet-number space used for 1-RTT protected packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a separate 0-RTT packet-number space is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-number allocation and acknowledgment state can be inspected to confirm shared space membership.

requirements.quote:
After a client receives a Retry packet, 0-RTT packets are likely to
   have been lost or discarded by the server.  A client SHOULD attempt
   to resend data in 0-RTT packets after it sends a new Initial packet.
   New packet numbers MUST be used for any new packets that are sent; as
   described in Section 17.2.5.3, reusing packet numbers could
   compromise packet protection.
requirements.condition: After a client receives a Retry packet and sends a new Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The client should attempt to resend the data in 0-RTT packets.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver Retry, observe the new Initial, and determine whether the client attempts 0-RTT data retransmission.

requirements.quote:
After a client receives a Retry packet, 0-RTT packets are likely to
   have been lost or discarded by the server.  A client SHOULD attempt
   to resend data in 0-RTT packets after it sends a new Initial packet.
   New packet numbers MUST be used for any new packets that are sent; as
   described in Section 17.2.5.3, reusing packet numbers could
   compromise packet protection.
requirements.condition: When sending any new packet after receipt of a Retry packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a new packet number for every new packet sent.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reusing a packet number for a new packet is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet traces can detect packet-number reuse, and the text directly identifies reuse as compromising packet protection.

requirements.quote:
A client only receives acknowledgments for its 0-RTT packets once the
   handshake is complete, as defined in Section 4.1.1 of [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A client must not receive acknowledgments for its 0-RTT packets.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake state and acknowledgment reception can be correlated in a protocol trace.

requirements.quote:
A client MUST NOT send 0-RTT packets once it starts processing 1-RTT
   packets from the server.  This means that 0-RTT packets cannot
   contain any response to frames from 1-RTT packets.  For instance, a
   client cannot send an ACK frame in a 0-RTT packet, because that can
   only acknowledge a 1-RTT packet.  An acknowledgment for a 1-RTT
   packet MUST be carried in a 1-RTT packet.
requirements.condition: Once a client starts processing 1-RTT packets from the server.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not send any 0-RTT packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-processing and transmission traces can verify that no 0-RTT transmission follows the first processed server 1-RTT packet.

requirements.quote:
A client MUST NOT send 0-RTT packets once it starts processing 1-RTT
   packets from the server.  This means that 0-RTT packets cannot
   contain any response to frames from 1-RTT packets.  For instance, a
   client cannot send an ACK frame in a 0-RTT packet, because that can
   only acknowledge a 1-RTT packet.  An acknowledgment for a 1-RTT
   packet MUST be carried in a 1-RTT packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The packet must not contain a response to any frame received in a 1-RTT packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Received 1-RTT frames can be correlated with the contents and semantics of subsequently constructed packets.

requirements.quote:
A client MUST NOT send 0-RTT packets once it starts processing 1-RTT
   packets from the server.  This means that 0-RTT packets cannot
   contain any response to frames from 1-RTT packets.  For instance, a
   client cannot send an ACK frame in a 0-RTT packet, because that can
   only acknowledge a 1-RTT packet.  An acknowledgment for a 1-RTT
   packet MUST be carried in a 1-RTT packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry the acknowledgment in a 1-RTT packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Carrying the acknowledgment in a 0-RTT packet is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet traces can verify the protection level of every packet carrying an acknowledgment for a 1-RTT packet.

requirements.quote:
A client MUST NOT send 0-RTT packets once it starts processing 1-RTT
   packets from the server.  This means that 0-RTT packets cannot
   contain any response to frames from 1-RTT packets.  For instance, a
   client cannot send an ACK frame in a 0-RTT packet, because that can
   only acknowledge a 1-RTT packet.  An acknowledgment for a 1-RTT
   packet MUST be carried in a 1-RTT packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include an ACK frame, because such an ACK can only acknowledge a 1-RTT packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A decoder can inspect 0-RTT packet payloads for ACK frames.

requirements.quote:
A server SHOULD treat a violation of remembered limits
   (Section 7.4.1) as a connection error of an appropriate type (for
   instance, a FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR for exceeding stream data limits).
requirements.condition: When a server detects a violation of remembered limits.
requirements.error_behavior: The server should treat the violation as a connection error of an appropriate type, such as FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR when stream data limits are exceeded.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can violate a remembered limit and inspect whether the server closes the connection with an error type appropriate to that limit.
